## Vấn Đề #5: Prediction Interval — Quá Rộng = Vô Dụng, Quá Hẹp = Sai

**Industry benchmark** từ [FinOps Foundation](https://www.finops.org/wg/cloud-cost-forecasting/):
- 1 tháng: ±5-10% MAPE cho stable workloads
- 3 tháng: ±8-15% MAPE
- 12 tháng: ±15-25% MAPE

### 5a. Conformal Prediction — Guaranteed Coverage

Proven bởi [Bellman Conformal Inference (BCI)](https://github.com/ZitongYang/bellman-conformal-inference), [Nixtla StatsForecast](https://nixtlaverse.nixtla.io/statsforecast/docs/tutorials/conformalprediction.html), và [MAPIE library](https://towardsdatascience.com/time-series-forecasting-with-conformal-prediction-intervals-scikit-learn-is-all-you-need-4b68143a027a/).

```
Khác biệt với traditional PI:

Traditional PI (SARIMA/ETS):
  Giả định: errors ~ Normal(0, σ²)
  PI = Ŷ ± 1.96σ
  ⚠ Nếu errors KHÔNG normal → coverage sai
  ⚠ Token usage errors thường RIGHT-SKEWED (spike dễ hơn dip)

Conformal Prediction:
  KHÔNG giả định distribution nào cả
  Dùng ACTUAL errors từ validation set
  
  Bước:
    1. Train model trên [day 1-120]
    2. Predict [day 121-150], tính residuals: e_i = Y_i - Ŷ_i
    3. Sort |e₁|, |e₂|, ..., |e₃₀| 
    4. q₉₅ = quantile(|e|, 0.95) = the 95th percentile of |errors|
    5. Future PI: Ŷ ± q₉₅
    
  → GUARANTEED: 95% future values sẽ nằm trong interval
  → Không cần giả định normality
  → Tự động widen nếu model kém, narrow nếu model tốt
```

### 5b. Asymmetric Intervals — Token Usage Đặc Thù

```
Token usage thường:
  - Có thể spike +50% (deadline, incident)
  - Hiếm khi drop -50% (team không thể làm việc -50%)
  
→ Interval KHÔNG nên symmetric!

Conformal với asymmetric quantiles:
  q_lower = quantile(e_negative, 0.025)  → negative residuals
  q_upper = quantile(e_positive, 0.975)  → positive residuals
  
  PI = [Ŷ + q_lower, Ŷ + q_upper]
  
  VD: q_lower = -80K, q_upper = +150K
  → PI = [Ŷ - 80K, Ŷ + 150K]
  → Upside risk wider than downside — realistic!
```

### 5c. Horizon-Dependent Interval Expansion

```
Naive approach: σ(h) = σ₁ × √h (square-root scaling)
  30 days: σ × √30 = 5.5σ → quá rộng

Better approach (empirical scaling):
  Tính ACTUAL error at each horizon from CV:
    MAPE(h=1) = 5%
    MAPE(h=7) = 8%
    MAPE(h=14) = 11%
    MAPE(h=30) = 15%
    MAPE(h=90) = 22%
  
  Fit power law: MAPE(h) = α × h^β
  VD: MAPE(h) = 5% × h^0.32
  
  → Interval width = Ŷ × MAPE(h) × z_score
  → Calibrated to ACTUAL performance, not theory
```

## Vấn Đề #6: Token ≠ Money — Cần Convert Chính Xác

```
Anthropic pricing (thay đổi theo model):
  Claude Sonnet:  Input $3/Mtok, Output $15/Mtok
  Claude Opus:    Input $15/Mtok, Output $75/Mtok
  Claude Haiku:   Input $0.25/Mtok, Output $1.25/Mtok

⚠ Data bạn có: TỔNG tokens per day
⚠ Nhưng cost = f(model_mix, input/output_ratio)

Giải pháp: Effective Token (ET) metric
  (Từ GitHub Blog — github.blog)
  
  ET = Σ (tokens_model_i × cost_multiplier_i)

    Haiku: 0.083x (input), 0.083x (output)
    Sonnet: 1.0x
    Opus: 5.0x
    
Nếu bạn CÓ breakdown theo model:
  → Predict mỗi model riêng → sum weighted cost
  
Nếu bạn CHỈ CÓ tổng tokens:
  → Giả định model_mix stable (kiểm tra từ invoices)
  → weighted_avg_cost_per_token = Σ(share_i × price_i)
  → Cost forecast = token_forecast × weighted_avg_cost_per_token
  
  ⚠ Risk: Anthropic thay đổi pricing → cost forecast sai
  → Thêm pricing_scenario: current / +20% / -20%
```

## Vấn Đề #7: Validation — Làm Sao Biết Forecast Thật Sự Tốt?

### 7a. Walk-Forward Validation (Gold Standard)

```
KHÔNG PHẢI chỉ chạy CV 1 lần. Phải test:
  "Nếu tôi đứng ở ngày 120, forecast 30 ngày tiếp theo có đúng không?"
  "Nếu tôi đứng ở ngày 90, forecast 30 ngày tiếp theo có đúng không?"

Walk-forward (origin shifting):
  Origin 1: Train [1-60],   Forecast [61-90],   Compare actual → MAPE₁
  Origin 2: Train [1-70],   Forecast [71-100],  Compare actual → MAPE₂
  Origin 3: Train [1-80],   Forecast [81-110],  Compare actual → MAPE₃
  Origin 4: Train [1-90],   Forecast [91-120],  Compare actual → MAPE₄
  Origin 5: Train [1-100],  Forecast [101-130], Compare actual → MAPE₅
  Origin 6: Train [1-110],  Forecast [111-140], Compare actual → MAPE₆
  Origin 7: Train [1-120],  Forecast [121-150], Compare actual → MAPE₇
  
  Avg MAPE = mean(MAPE₁..₇) → expected accuracy of model
  Std MAPE = std(MAPE₁..₇)  → stability of model
  
  ⚠ Nếu MAPE₇ >> MAPE₁ → model deteriorating → regime change possible
```

### 7b. Naive Baselines — Model Phải Beat These

```
Seasonal Naive: Ŷ(t+h) = Y(t+h-7)  
  "Tuần tới giống tuần này"
  → Surprisingly accurate! MAPE ≈ 12-18% cho enterprise token usage

Random Walk: Ŷ(t+h) = Y(t)
  "Ngày mai giống hôm nay"
  → MAPE ≈ 15-25%

Historical Mean: Ŷ(t+h) = mean(Y)
  → MAPE ≈ 25-40%

MASE (Mean Absolute Scaled Error):
  MASE = MAE_model / MAE_naive_seasonal
  
  MASE < 1.0 → model TỐT HƠN naive → worth using
  MASE > 1.0 → model TỆ HƠN naive → BỎ ĐI, dùng naive
  MASE = 0.5 → model tốt gấp đôi naive
  
  Target: MASE < 0.7 cho 30-day forecast
```

### 7c. Diebold-Mariano Test — Model A Có Thực Sự Tốt Hơn Model B?

```
Khi so sánh 2 models:
  d(t) = |e_A(t)| - |e_B(t)|  (difference in absolute errors)
  
  DM statistic = mean(d) / (σ_d / √n)
  
  Nếu DM significant (p < 0.05) → khác biệt THẬT
  Nếu DM không significant → cả hai models tương đương → dùng ensemble
  
  ⚠ Quan trọng: "Model A có MAPE 10%, model B có MAPE 12%"
  → KHÔNG CHẮC A tốt hơn B! Có thể chỉ do randomness
  → DM test cho biết chắc chắn
```

## Vấn Đề #8: Year Forecast — Khi Extrapolation Là Speculation

**Thực tế nghiệt ngã:** FinOps Foundation benchmark cho long-term (12-36 tháng) = ±15-25% MAPE. Với 5 tháng data, realistic target là ±20-30%.

### 8a. Monte Carlo Simulation — "10,000 Tương Lai Có Thể"

```
Thay vì 1 forecast line, simulate 10,000 possible futures:

For each simulation i = 1 to 10,000:
  1. Sample trend slope từ posterior distribution
  2. Sample seasonal pattern (add noise to seasonal indices)
  3. Sample random shocks (from empirical error distribution)
  4. Generate 365 ngày: Y(t) = trend(t) + seasonal(t) + shock(t)
  5. Sum → annual_tokens_i

Output:
  P10 (conservative): quantile(annual_tokens, 0.10)
  P50 (baseline): quantile(annual_tokens, 0.50)  
  P90 (aggressive): quantile(annual_tokens, 0.90)
  Mean: mean(annual_tokens)
  
  + Probability of exceeding budget X:
    P(annual > X) = count(annual_tokens > X) / 10,000
```

### 8b. Scenario Trees — Business Context

```
Monte Carlo giả định "tương lai giống quá khứ".
NHƯNG enterprise có planned events:

Year forecast = Base statistical forecast × Business adjustment

Business adjustments (manual input):
  Q3: Team tăng 2 → usage × 1.25
  Q4: New product launch → usage × 1.40 for 2 months, then × 1.15
  December holiday → usage × 0.60 for 2 weeks
  
Scenario tree:
  Base × (no change)
  Base × (team grows) × (product launch) × (holiday)
  Base × (team grows) × (no product launch) × (holiday)
  
  Mỗi scenario gán probability:
    P(team grows Q3) = 0.70
    P(product launch Q4) = 0.40
    P(holiday pattern) = 0.95
    
  Expected annual = Σ P(scenario_i) × forecast(scenario_i)
```

## Kết Nối Tất Cả: Pipeline Hoàn Chỉnh Đã Được Chứng Minh

```
STAGE 1: DATA QUALITY
  → Outlier detection (IQR + Z-score)
  → Missing imputation (linear interpolation)
  → Changepoint detection (PELT via ruptures)
  → Stationarity test (ADF + KPSS)
  → Weekly pattern stability test
  → Trend significance test (Mann-Kendall)
  
STAGE 2: TEMPORAL HIERARCHY
  → Generate 5 aggregation levels (daily/3-day/weekly/biweekly/monthly)
  → Fit models at each level independently
  → Reconcile via MinTrace (hierarchicalforecast)
  
STAGE 3: MULTI-MODEL ENSEMBLE  
  Level 1 (daily): SARIMA + ETS + XGBoost
  Level 3 (weekly): ETS + Theta
  Level 5 (monthly): SES
  + Cross-level: BSTS + GP
  → Walk-forward validation per model per horizon
  → Inverse-MAPE weighting (horizon-adaptive)
  → Beat naive baseline test (MASE < 0.7)
  
STAGE 4: UNCERTAINTY CALIBRATION
  → Conformal prediction (asymmetric intervals)
  → Horizon-dependent scaling (empirical power law)
  → Coverage back-test (target 95%)
  
STAGE 5: BUSINESS OVERLAY
  → Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 futures)
  → Scenario trees (business events)
  → Token-to-cost conversion (model mix weighted)
  → Pricing scenarios (current / ±20%)

OUTPUT ACCURACY TARGETS (based on FinOps benchmarks):
  Next month:   MAPE 5-10%, 95% CI ≈ ±15%
  Next quarter: MAPE 8-15%, 95% CI ≈ ±25%
  Next year:    MAPE 15-25%, 3 scenarios (P10/P50/P90)
```

**Date:** 2026-06-02
**Type:** Brainstorm / Algorithm Design
**Status:** Research Complete — Ready for Implementation Planning

---

## Problem Statement

- **Input:** 5 months (~150 days) daily aggregate token usage data (enterprise, Claude AI)
- **Output:** Point estimates + confidence intervals for next month, quarter, year
- **Constraint:** 150 datapoints = statistical models only, no deep learning
- **Data format:** Private database, daily aggregation

## Accuracy Targets (FinOps Foundation Benchmarks)

| Horizon | Target MAPE | Target 95% CI Width | Approach |
|---------|-------------|---------------------|----------|
| Next month (30d) | 5-10% | ±15% | Ensemble of 6 models |
| Next quarter (90d) | 8-15% | ±25% | Ensemble + temporal hierarchy |
| Next year (365d) | 15-25% | P10/P50/P90 scenarios | Monte Carlo + business overlay |

**"Absolute precision" is mathematically impossible for any forecast.** Best achievable: tightest possible CI with calibrated coverage.

---

## Architecture: 5-Stage Pipeline

```
STAGE 1: DATA QUALITY
  → Outlier detection (IQR + Z-score > 3)
  → Missing day imputation (linear interpolation)
  → Changepoint detection (PELT via ruptures library)
  → Stationarity test (ADF + KPSS dual test)
  → Weekly pattern stability test (5-block SI comparison)
  → Trend significance test (Mann-Kendall + Theil-Sen slope)

STAGE 2: TEMPORAL HIERARCHY
  → Generate 5 aggregation levels:
    Level 1: Daily (150 pts)
    Level 2: 3-day (50 pts)
    Level 3: Weekly (21 pts)
    Level 4: Bi-weekly (10 pts)
    Level 5: Monthly (5 pts)
  → Fit models at each level independently
  → Reconcile via MinTrace (Nixtla/hierarchicalforecast)

STAGE 3: MULTI-MODEL ENSEMBLE
  → 6 base models (see detail below)
  → Walk-forward validation per model per horizon
  → Inverse-MAPE weighting (horizon-adaptive)
  → Beat naive baseline test (MASE < 0.7 required)

STAGE 4: UNCERTAINTY CALIBRATION
  → Conformal prediction (asymmetric intervals)
  → Horizon-dependent scaling (empirical power law)
  → Coverage back-test (target 95% actual coverage)

STAGE 5: BUSINESS OVERLAY
  → Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 futures)
  → Scenario trees (business events: team growth, holidays)
  → Token-to-cost conversion (model mix weighted)
  → Pricing scenarios (current / ±20%)
```

---

## 8 Sub-Problems Decomposition

### Sub-Problem #1: Small Dataset (150 Days)

**Solutions:**
1. **Temporal Aggregation (MAPA)** — Convert 1 series to 5 at different frequencies. Proven by Kourentzes & Petropoulos (2014). Reconcile via MinTrace.
2. **Moving Block Bootstrap** — Generate 100 synthetic series preserving weekly structure. block_size=7. Proven by Bandara et al. (2021, arXiv:2008.02663).
3. **Multi-Resolution Feature Stacking** — Extract 15+ features from each datapoint (lags, rolling stats, momentum, volatility).

### Sub-Problem #2: Weekly Pattern Extraction

**Solutions:**
1. **STL Decomposition (Robust)** — LOESS-based, handles evolving seasonality. `robust=True` required for token data outliers.
2. **Fourier Terms** — K=2-3 harmonics, fewer parameters than dummies → less overfitting.
3. **Stability Test** — 5-block SI comparison. CV < 5% = stable (use global), CV > 15% = evolving (use STL adaptive).

### Sub-Problem #3: Trend Estimation

**Solutions:**
1. **Theil-Sen Estimator** — Median-based slope, robust to outliers.
2. **Mann-Kendall Test** — Significance test before including trend. p > 0.05 → forecast flat.
3. **Damping Factor Selection** — Cross-validation over φ ∈ {0.80, 0.85, 0.90, 0.95, 1.00}. Domain: stable teams φ=0.85-0.90, growing teams φ=0.92-0.97.

### Sub-Problem #4: Regime Change Detection

**Solutions:**
1. **PELT Algorithm** — Exact changepoint detection in linear time. Via `ruptures` library. Penalty: BIC (conservative).
2. **Post-Detection Strategy:**
   - Truncate (use only post-changepoint data)
   - Weight (exponential decay on old data)
   - BSTS (automatic via σ²_μ posterior)
   - Piecewise (fit model per regime if each >28 days)

### Sub-Problem #5: Prediction Interval Calibration

**Solutions:**
1. **Conformal Prediction** — Distribution-free, guaranteed coverage. Via MAPIE or Nixtla StatsForecast.
2. **Asymmetric Intervals** — Token usage right-skewed (spikes > dips). Use separate quantiles for upper/lower.
3. **Horizon Scaling** — Fit empirical power law: MAPE(h) = α × h^β from walk-forward CV, not theoretical √h.

### Sub-Problem #6: Token-to-Cost Conversion

**Solution:** Effective Token (ET) metric with model-specific multipliers.
```
ET = Σ (tokens_model_i × cost_multiplier_i)
Haiku: 0.083x, Sonnet: 1.0x, Opus: 5.0x
```
If only total tokens available, use weighted_avg_cost_per_token from invoice breakdown.

### Sub-Problem #7: Validation Framework

**Solutions:**
1. **Walk-Forward Validation** — 7 origins, 30-day forecast each. Avg MAPE + Std MAPE.
2. **Naive Baselines** — Seasonal naive (MAPE ~12-18%), random walk, historical mean. Model MUST beat MASE < 1.0.
3. **Diebold-Mariano Test** — Statistical test for model comparison significance.

### Sub-Problem #8: Year Forecast (Speculation Zone)

**Solutions:**
1. **Monte Carlo Simulation** — 10,000 futures sampling from trend/seasonal/noise posteriors.
2. **Scenario Trees** — Business events (team growth, product launches, holidays) with probabilities.
3. **Output as P10/P50/P90** — Never a single number for year forecast.

---

## 6 Base Models — Detailed Specifications

### Model 1: SARIMA(X) — statsmodels.tsa.statespace.SARIMAX

```
SARIMA(p,d,q)(P,D,Q,7) with exogenous variables

Parameter selection: Grid search, minimize BIC
  p,q ∈ [0,3], d ∈ [0,1]
  P,Q ∈ [0,2], D ∈ [0,1], m = 7

Exogenous: is_weekend, is_holiday, is_month_end, day_of_week

Strength: Best short-term (1-14 days), exploits autocorrelation directly
Weakness: Degrades >60 days, assumes linear relationships
```

### Model 2: ETS Holt-Winters (Damped, Multiplicative) — statsmodels.tsa.holtwinters

```
ETS(M,Ad,M): Multiplicative error + Additive damped trend + Multiplicative seasonal

Level:    L(t) = α · Y(t)/S(t-m) + (1-α) · (L(t-1) + φ·T(t-1))
Trend:    T(t) = β · (L(t) - L(t-1)) + (1-β) · φ·T(t-1)
Season:   S(t) = γ · Y(t)/L(t) + (1-γ) · S(t-m)
Forecast: Ŷ(t+h) = (L(t) + Σᵢ₌₁ʰ φⁱ·T(t)) · S(t+h-m·⌈h/m⌉)

α,β,γ ∈ (0,1), φ ∈ (0.80, 0.98), m=7
Optimized via MLE

Strength: Stable across all horizons, damping prevents divergence
Weakness: Assumes fixed seasonal shape (mitigated by γ)
```

### Model 3: Theta Method — statsmodels.tsa.forecasting.theta.ThetaModel

```
1. STL decompose → trend + seasonal + residual
2. Apply theta lines: θ=0 (linear extrapolation) + θ=2 (double curvature)
3. Forecast each with SES
4. Combine: Ŷ = 0.5·Ŷ(θ=0) + 0.5·Ŷ(θ=2)
5. Re-seasonalize

Strength: Won M3 competition, dead simple, robust
Weakness: No exogenous variables
```

### Model 4: BSTS — pyro or tensorflow_probability

```
Observation: Y(t) = μ(t) + τ(t) + β·X(t) + ε(t)
Local level: μ(t) = μ(t-1) + δ(t-1) + η_μ(t)
Local trend: δ(t) = δ(t-1) + η_δ(t)
Seasonality: τ(t) = -Σⱼ₌₁⁶ τ(t-j) + η_τ(t)

Priors:
  σ²_obs ~ InverseGamma(5, mean(Y)²×0.01)
  σ²_μ ~ InverseGamma(10, mean(Y)²×0.001)
  σ²_δ ~ InverseGamma(20, mean(Y)²×0.0001)
  σ²_τ ~ InverseGamma(15, mean(Y)²×0.0005)

Inference: MCMC Gibbs (5000-10000 samples, burn-in 1000-2000, thin 5)

Strength: Best uncertainty quantification, regime change handling, prior injection
Weakness: Computationally expensive, requires prior tuning
```

### Model 5: Gaussian Process — sklearn.gaussian_process

```
Kernel: k_RQ(trend) + k_Periodic(weekly) + k_Periodic(monthly) + k_noise

k_RQ: σ²(1 + |t-t'|²/(2α·ℓ²))^(-α), ℓ≈60-90, α≈2-5
k_weekly: σ²·exp(-2sin²(π|t-t'|/7)/ℓ²), ℓ≈1.0-2.0
k_monthly: σ²·exp(-2sin²(π|t-t'|/30.44)/ℓ²)
k_noise: σ²·δ(t,t')

Hyperparameters: 8 total, optimized via marginal likelihood (L-BFGS-B)

Strength: Non-parametric, natural uncertainty growth, perfect for n=150
Weakness: Poor with abrupt regime changes, kernel must be designed correctly
```

### Model 6: Gradient Boosted Trees — sklearn.ensemble.GradientBoostingRegressor

```
Features (18+):
  Temporal: day_of_week, is_weekend, is_holiday, day_of_month, week_of_month, month
  Lag: lag_1, lag_2, lag_7, lag_14, lag_28
  Rolling: rolling_mean_7, rolling_mean_14, rolling_mean_28, rolling_std_7
  Derived: ewm_7, momentum_14d, trend (days_since_start)

Multi-step strategy: DIRECT (separate model per horizon h=1,7,30,90)
Validation: Expanding window CV (NEVER random split)

Strength: Captures non-linear interactions (month_end + high_momentum = spike)
Weakness: Recursive error compounds; use direct strategy for h>7
```

## Ensemble Weighting

### Inverse-MAPE Weighted Average

```
weight_i = (1/MAPE_i) / Σⱼ(1/MAPE_j)
Ŷ_ensemble = Σᵢ weight_i × Ŷ_i

Uncertainty (compound):
  σ²_total = σ²_within (model intervals) + σ²_between (model disagreement)
  95% PI: Ŷ ± 1.96 × √σ²_total
```

| Model | h=1-30d | h=31-90d | h=91-365d |
|-------|---------|----------|-----------|
